modules.title: Engineering readiness
modules.label: Optional readiness bridge
modules.summary: Bring your existing engineering experience into a common working environment.
topics: API contracts, HTTP, JSON, and asynchronous requests
Relational data modelling and SQL
Git workflows, unit tests, and dependency isolation
Service configuration, containers, and cloud fundamentals
tools: Python — reference backend language
FastAPI + Pydantic — typed service contracts
PostgreSQL — application data
pytest + Git — repeatable checks and versioned work
modules.practice: Connect a small React client to a Python service and a database. Introduce an unavailable dependency, return a useful error, and add a regression test.
deliverables: A running service-integration exercise
A request/data-flow diagram
Setup instructions and boundary-case tests
criteria: Another engineer can run the exercise from its README
Invalid input is rejected at the API boundary
A failed dependency is handled and tested
modules.question: What changes when a dependency is slow instead of unavailable?

modules.title: AI application engineering
modules.label: Ground answers in evidence
modules.summary: Build applications that use model capabilities deliberately and retrieve the right evidence.
topics: LLM behaviour, context windows, prompts, and context engineering
Validated structured outputs and tool arguments
Embeddings, chunking, metadata, and document ingestion
Retrieval quality, source citations, abstention, and updates
tools: Model API — generation and embeddings, called server-side
Pydantic — output validation
PostgreSQL + pgvector — permission-filtered retrieval
Python + pytest — ingestion and evaluation cases
modules.practice: Build a document assistant over sample policies. Compare two chunking approaches on the same questions, then test an unsupported question and a restricted document.
deliverables: An ingestion and retrieval pipeline
Cited answers and explicit insufficient-evidence responses
A small evaluation dataset and retrieval comparison
criteria: Citations refer to supporting source passages
Restricted evidence never reaches an unauthorised request
Unsupported questions do not produce invented answers
modules.question: How would you tell whether a wrong answer began with retrieval or generation?

modules.title: Agents and multimodal applications
modules.label: Knowledge becomes supervised action
modules.summary: Coordinate tools and people, then extend the interaction beyond typed text.
topics: State, tasks, memory, tool contracts, and bounded execution
MCP tools, resources, and integration boundaries
Human approval, retries, idempotency, and multi-agent tradeoffs
Speech-to-text, text-to-speech, vision, and document understanding
tools: LangGraph — stateful workflows, checkpoints, and approval
MCP — a standard interface to scoped tools and resources
Pydantic — validated tool inputs and outputs
Speech/vision model APIs — transcription and document interpretation
modules.practice: Build a request workflow that prepares a proposed update and pauses for approval. Add a small speech or document-image input exercise, retaining a visible transcript or extracted evidence for review.
deliverables: A workflow state diagram and approval demonstration
A scoped MCP adapter using a simulated tool
A multimodal exercise with uncertainty and fallback handling
criteria: A rejected action does not execute
Retries do not duplicate completed actions
Step limits stop a looping workflow
Low-confidence extracted content is surfaced for review
modules.question: When does splitting a task across agents add value over a deterministic pipeline?

modules.title: Production AI engineering
modules.label: Measure, operate, improve
modules.summary: Move beyond a convincing demo to a system whose behaviour you can inspect.
topics: Evaluation datasets, regression checks, and failure analysis
Guardrails, prompt injection, privacy, and server-side secrets
Tracing, latency budgets, token cost, and operational signals
Docker, CI checks, release validation, and rollback
tools: Langfuse — traces and evaluation examples
pytest — regression tests and scoring assertions
Docker — repeatable application packaging
Git + CI workflow — tested changes and release checks
modules.practice: Run two application versions against the same dataset. Diagnose a failing trace, compare quality and cost, and rehearse a failed release followed by rollback in a learning environment.
deliverables: An evaluation report with observed results
Trace examples and an incident note
A containerised application and release checklist
criteria: Results can be reproduced on the same inputs
The report includes failures and limitations
Secrets are excluded from source and browser code
Rollback instructions are actionable
modules.question: What evidence would make you hold a release even if its average answer quality improved?

modules.title: Enterprise integration
modules.label: Fit the systems already in place
modules.summary: Connect AI to identity, data, and operational systems without losing their boundaries.
topics: OAuth/OIDC, identity propagation, and role-based access
REST APIs, databases, webhooks, and adapter contracts
SharePoint, CRM, ERP, and service-system integration patterns
Least privilege, audit events, rate limits, and legacy-system failures
tools: FastAPI — typed adapters and service boundaries
OAuth/OIDC + RBAC — identity and authorisation concepts
PostgreSQL — permitted records and audit receipts
MCP + fixture APIs — scoped enterprise integration exercises
modules.practice: Implement a read-only adapter for a simulated enterprise service. Propagate identity, deny a restricted record, and prepare a write proposal that requires explicit approval before simulated execution.
deliverables: An adapter contract and integration map
Allowed/denied access tests
An execution receipt and audit trail
criteria: Permissions are checked outside model-generated text
A denied request cannot disclose restricted content
Timeouts and rate limits have defined handling
A write requires authorised approval
modules.question: Why is a valid tool argument not enough to authorise an action?

modules.title: Solution architecture and forward deployment
modules.label: Own the delivery story
modules.summary: Frame the right problem, choose a defensible approach, and prepare another team to use it.
topics: Customer discovery, workflow mapping, and a measurable value case
RAG vs fine-tuning vs smaller models
Agents vs deterministic workflows; build vs integrate
Pilot acceptance, adoption, handover, and iteration planning
tools: Architecture diagrams — components, trust boundaries, and data flow
Evaluation reports — evidence for a pilot decision
Runbooks — deployment, recovery, and ownership
Python-led capstone — one integrated delivery case
modules.practice: Take an illustrative customer brief through discovery, architecture, an integrated pilot, evaluation, and handover. Explain a tradeoff to a technical reviewer and a non-technical stakeholder.
deliverables: A scoped problem statement and acceptance criteria
An integrated pilot and delivery case study
A deployment runbook and handover presentation
criteria: Success criteria connect to the stated user problem
The design explains why simpler alternatives were rejected
The demo covers a failure as well as a successful path
The handover names limitations and next decisions
modules.question: What would you measure before recommending that a pilot should expand?

modules.title: Retrieval quality & data operations
modules.label: Advanced retrieval lab
modules.summary: Keep a document assistant useful when its knowledge changes, access rules differ and retrieval is imperfect.
topics: Document provenance, versioning, duplicate detection and incremental ingestion
Permission filters and deleted or outdated source material
Keyword and vector retrieval comparisons using a labelled question set
Retrieval recall, citation relevance, answer support and latency tradeoffs
tools: PostgreSQL + pgvector — compare filtered vector retrieval with a SQL baseline
Python + Pydantic — validate document metadata and ingestion contracts
pytest — regression checks for updates, deletions and permission boundaries
Langfuse — compare evaluation runs and inspect unsuccessful answers
modules.practice: Extend the knowledge assistant with a versioned sample corpus. Update one document, remove another and restrict a third. Compare two retrieval strategies against a fixed question set, including questions the corpus cannot answer.
deliverables: A repeatable ingestion and refresh command
A labelled retrieval dataset with expected sources and access context
A comparison report covering quality, unsupported answers and response time
criteria: Re-running ingestion does not create duplicate document versions
Deleted or restricted evidence is absent from relevant test answers
Reported improvements include failures and the evaluation sample size
Retrieval limitations are explained without treating a score as proof of correctness
modules.question: How would you distinguish a retrieval failure from an answer-generation failure?

modules.title: Pilot delivery & operational handover
modules.label: Integrated delivery rehearsal
modules.summary: Bring the engineering work together in a small pilot that another team can evaluate, operate and improve.
topics: Pilot success criteria, baseline measures and acceptance scenarios
Release checklists, configuration boundaries and rollback decisions
Incident triage, dependency failures and budget controls
User feedback, adoption checks and ownership after handover
tools: FastAPI + React — deliver the pilot workflow and explain its user experience
Docker — package a repeatable demonstration environment
pytest + Git — run acceptance checks and identify the reviewed release
Langfuse — inspect traces and compare the pilot against its evaluation baseline
modules.practice: Run a simulated stakeholder review of the integrated capstone. Demonstrate its happy path, a denied action and an unavailable model service. Rehearse a rollback and ask another engineer to operate the pilot using only the handover pack.
deliverables: A working pilot demonstration with explicit scope and exclusions
An acceptance report with evaluation results and known limitations
A deployment runbook, rollback checklist and ownership map
A delivery case study linking the original problem to decisions and evidence
criteria: Another engineer can reproduce the demonstration from the runbook
Failure paths are visible and actions remain within approval boundaries
The go / revise / pause decision is supported by measurable evidence
Handover separates completed work from future improvements and unresolved risks
modules.question: What evidence would make you pause the pilot instead of recommending a wider rollout?

projects.title: Permission-aware knowledge assistant
projects.summary: Useful answers, grounded in the documents a person is allowed to see.
projects.problem: A service team searches scattered policies and ticket guidance. Some documents are restricted, sources disagree, and an unsupported answer can mislead the user.
projects.user: An internal service specialist looking for a sourced answer.
journey: Ask a policy question in the application.
Retrieve only documents permitted for that user.
Read the answer with supporting source passages.
See an explicit limitation when evidence is missing or conflicting.
responsibilities: React presents the question, citations, and limitation states.
FastAPI validates the request and applies authorisation.
The model composes an answer; evaluations inspect its grounding.
failures: A restricted document is relevant but must remain inaccessible.
No passage supports the requested answer.
An ingested document contains instructions that attempt to override the application.
evidence: Answerable, unanswerable, and restricted-source evaluation cases
A demo with citations and an insufficient-evidence response
projects.review: No restricted evidence reaches an unauthorised request; answers cite sources and acknowledge missing support.

projects.title: Approved operations workflow
projects.summary: Let AI prepare the next step. Keep authorisation explicit.
projects.problem: An operations request crosses several systems. A generated suggestion must not become an uncontrolled update, and retries must not duplicate an action.
projects.user: An operations reviewer deciding whether a proposed update should proceed.
journey: Submit a request against a sample enterprise-system fixture.
Inspect the gathered records and proposed change.
Review the execution receipt or the reason no action was taken.
responsibilities: LangGraph manages state, checkpoints, and the review boundary.
An MCP adapter exposes limited fixture tools.
Pydantic validates tool contracts; ordinary code enforces permissions.
A simulated service records idempotent execution and audit events.
failures: A tool times out after execution; a retry must not duplicate it.
An unauthorised request attempts to use a write tool.
evidence: A state diagram and approval walkthrough
Denied, rejected, timeout, and duplicate-request tests
A scoped adapter contract and execution receipts
projects.review: Generated text is never treated as authorisation. A rejected action cannot execute and a retry cannot duplicate an approved update.

projects.title: From customer brief to AI pilot
projects.summary: Connect the system, the evidence, and the handover into one coherent delivery story.
projects.problem: A team has an AI idea but needs to know whether it helps a defined workflow and what operating it would require.
projects.user: A pilot sponsor and the engineers who would maintain the solution.
journey: Agree a narrow problem, user group, and acceptance criteria.
Demonstrate an integrated knowledge or action workflow.
Inspect quality, failure cases, latency, and cost evidence.
Rehearse deployment and recovery in a learning environment.
Present a recommendation with limitations and next steps.
responsibilities: Python services and React deliver the user workflow.
PostgreSQL and scoped adapters provide application context.
Langfuse and test cases provide operational and quality evidence.
Docker, release notes, and a runbook support the handover.
failures: The pilot misses one acceptance criterion.
A dependency becomes unavailable during the demonstration.
A proposed improvement adds cost without useful quality gains.
evidence: A discovery brief and architecture decision record
Deployment checklist, rollback notes, and delivery case study
projects.review: The recommendation follows the evidence, including gaps. Another engineer can understand the deployment, recovery steps, and remaining limitations.
